title: Etiquette & language
body:
Japan is a no-tipping culture — leaving cash on the table causes confusion, and staff have been known to chase guests down to return it. Service is already priced in.

At izakaya, an unrequested small starter (otoshi, a few hundred yen per person) lands on the table automatically and appears on the bill — it isn't a scam or an optional order. Calling "sumimasen" to get a server's attention is normal; nobody comes to the table unprompted the way US service does.

Chopstick basics: never stick them upright in a rice bowl, never pass food chopstick-to-chopstick, and use the opposite end (or provided serving chopsticks) when taking from a shared plate. Shoes come off before stepping onto tatami seating, common at traditional and izakaya spots.

Situational phrases for the trip — allergy/dietary, reservations, ordering — are on the Trip Kit tab.
